links.reading: William, your steady attention can help Charlotte feel safe enough to share what she likes. Charlotte, you may welcome his care while still wanting to choose for yourself. This contact can make small acts of affection feel dependable, not demanding. Behaviour check: This week, notice whether William’s help leaves Charlotte room to choose.

William, your practical help can meet Charlotte’s wish to do part of the morning routine herself. Charlotte, you may enjoy his support and still want to manage your own task. This easy cooperation can cost you time if William steps in before asking. Behaviour check: In the morning rush, let Charlotte choose one task before William helps.

William, you may hold a firm bedtime limit when the evening is already busy. Charlotte, you may resist if the decision feels settled before you can explain your concern. Your strong wills can turn a small limit into a longer standoff. Behaviour check: At bedtime, William asks what is bothering Charlotte before repeating the limit.

William, you may hear Charlotte’s homework answer as clearer than she meant it. Charlotte, you may find your thoughts hard to explain while someone is correcting you. A quick guess can leave you both talking past each other. Behaviour check: At the kitchen table, William asks Charlotte to explain her thinking before correcting an answer.

William, you may expect Charlotte to enjoy a plan because you meant it kindly. Charlotte, you may want something different but hesitate to say so. Then a kind offer can feel like pressure, even when neither of you meant it that way. Behaviour check: This week, William asks Charlotte whether she wants the offer before making plans.

William, your sudden change of plan may interrupt Charlotte while she is explaining herself. Charlotte, you may answer sharply when you feel rushed or unheard. The quick exchange can leave the original question unanswered. Behaviour check: This week, pause once during a disagreement and let Charlotte finish her sentence.

William, you can set a clear tablet limit without ending the conversation. Charlotte, you can suggest a fair plan when you know what the limit is. This works best when the rule comes early and your choice is real. Behaviour check: With the tablet, William states the limit early and lets Charlotte choose when to stop within it.

William, you may want the evening to follow a settled routine. Charlotte, you may want to change the order or do one part your way. A firm plan can help, but too little choice can make Charlotte push back. Behaviour check: At bedtime, agree together which part of the routine Charlotte can choose.

William, your strong concern can make Charlotte feel that you notice when something is wrong. Charlotte, you may feel deeply about family matters but need time before explaining them. Your attention can comfort her, though pressing for an answer may make her withdraw. Behaviour check: At bedtime, William asks whether Charlotte wants comfort or a little time alone.

William, you may change a routine quickly when a new idea seems useful. Charlotte, you may prefer to know what is expected before adjusting. Your plans can work well when change has a clear reason, but sudden shifts may unsettle her. Behaviour check: Before changing a routine this week, William tells Charlotte what is changing and asks what she thinks.
